Usage 

library(damR)
exdata_path <- list.files(
  system.file(package = "damR", "extdata"),
  "example_data.csv",
  full.names = TRUE
)

Load and clean data

ReadFile() expects a wide-format dataset where the rows are samples and columns are metabolites.

read.csv(exdata_path)[1:10, 1:5]
#>         Sample Histidine_IP Glycine_IP Serine_IP Asparagine_IP
#> 1  S01a_A-B_01     45579054   76592811  38007391       4580929
#> 2  S01b_A-C_01     13072561   24625238  17531599       1551767
#> 3  S01c_A-D_01      4312298    7852034   6420602        289036
#> 4  S01d_A-E_01      1928348    1652953        NA         68157
#> 5  S02a_A-B_02     43441954   70070730  32944539       4117218
#> 6  S02b_A-C_02     14035246   26371310  16108976       1569177
#> 7  S02c_A-D_02      4481968    9056500   6310596        426139
#> 8  S02d_A-E_02      2350293    2699275   2089174        145032
#> 9  S03a_A-B_03     45869650   79937601  37503859       4729428
#> 10 S03b_A-C_03     14058030   25090665  16919752       1527971

The Sample column should be in the form SampleID_Subgroup1ID-Subgroup2ID_BatchNo to infer Sample, Group, Subgroup, and Batch identifiers based on the “_” and “-” delimiters. The Metabolite column must be in the form MetaboliteName_ExtractionMethod for filtering based on extraction method (IP/HILIC/T3Acidic).

(mdata <- ReadFile(exdata_path))
#>              Sample SampleID   Group Subgroup1 Subgroup2  Batch    Metabolite
#>              <char>   <char>  <char>    <char>    <char> <char>        <char>
#>     1:  S01a_A-B_01     S01a     A_B         A         B     01     Histidine
#>     2:  S01b_A-C_01     S01b     A_C         A         C     01     Histidine
#>     3:  S01c_A-D_01     S01c     A_D         A         D     01     Histidine
#>     4:  S01d_A-E_01     S01d     A_E         A         E     01     Histidine
#>     5:  S02a_A-B_02     S02a     A_B         A         B     02     Histidine
#>    ---                                                                       
#> 16096: TC_QC-pool_2       TC QC_pool        QC      pool      2 D-Sphingosine
#> 16097: TC_QC-pool_3       TC QC_pool        QC      pool      3 D-Sphingosine
#> 16098: TC_QC-pool_4       TC QC_pool        QC      pool      4 D-Sphingosine
#> 16099: TC_QC-pool_5       TC QC_pool        QC      pool      5 D-Sphingosine
#> 16100: TC_QC-pool_6       TC QC_pool        QC      pool      6 D-Sphingosine
#>            Type    value
#>          <char>    <num>
#>     1:       IP 25.44187
#>     2:       IP 23.64004
#>     3:       IP 22.04003
#>     4:       IP 20.87893
#>     5:       IP 25.37259
#>    ---                  
#> 16096: T3Acidic 21.97819

#> 16100: T3Acidic 18.42540

ReadFile() pivots the data from wide to long or tidy form for the rest of the analysis.

QC

Each metabolite in the dataset may be sampled with multiple extraction methods. For each metabolite, FilterExtraction() selects the method with the fewest NAs or the lowest variation. FilterBlanks() runs blank filtering to remove metabolites from non-blank samples that fail to meet a specified fold-change threshold compared to the same metabolites from blank samples. To identify the data that get blank filtered without running the filtering, use GetBlankDropTable() which FilterBlanks() uses to identify the metabolites to remove as well as the blank samples.

QCData is a top-level function that calls both FilterExtraction() and FilterBlanks(), and removes metabolites with low variance.

to_drop <- GetBlankDropTable(mdata)
head(to_drop$dropTable)
#>     Batch       Sample SampleID   Group Subgroup1 Subgroup2    Metabolite
#>    <char>       <char>   <char>  <char>    <char>    <char>        <char>
#> 1:      1 TC_QC-pool_1       TC QC_pool        QC      pool  Hypoxanthine
#> 2:      1 TC_QC-pool_1       TC QC_pool        QC      pool      Xanthine
#> 3:      1 TC_QC-pool_1       TC QC_pool        QC      pool  Deoxyuridine
#> 4:      1 TC_QC-pool_1       TC QC_pool        QC      pool       Adenine
#> 5:      1 TC_QC-pool_1       TC QC_pool        QC      pool Phenylalanine
#> 6:      1 TC_QC-pool_1       TC QC_pool        QC      pool     Thymidine
#>      Type     value max_blank       diff
#>    <char>     <num>     <num>      <num>
#> 1:     IP  1.584963  1.000000  0.5849625
#> 2:     IP  1.000000  2.321928 -1.3219281
#> 3:     IP 11.315150  9.733015  1.5821342
#> 4:     IP 21.131802 18.927622  2.2041806
#> 5:     IP 18.291094 18.074695  0.2163987
#> 6:     IP  2.000000  1.000000  1.0000000
to_drop$blanks
#> [1] "TC_Blank-process_1" "TC_Blank-process_2" "TC_Blank-process_3"
#> [4] "TC_Blank-process_4" "TC_Blank-process_5"

qc_data <- QCData(mdata)

RemoveMissing() drops metabolites with more NAs than a specified proportion. To just get those that would be removed, use IdentifyMetabolites(). Use PlotMissingness to get a presence/absence heatmap of your data.

head(IdentifyMissing(qc_data))
#> [1] "2'-Deoxycytidine"           "2-Hydroxybutyrate"         
#> [3] "2-Methylcitrate"            "3-Hydroxyisobutyrate"      
#> [5] "3-Methyl-2-oxovaleric acid" "4-Hydroxybutyrate"
rm_data <- RemoveMissing(qc_data)

To examine your data before and after QC, you can use PCA. By default it returns a ggplot object but if ggiraph is available, setting interactive = TRUE and using ggiraph::girafe() to render the plot will produce an interactive plot.

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
ggiraph_available <- requireNamespace("ggiraph", quietly = TRUE)

pca.raw <- PlotPCA(GetPCA(mdata), interactive = ggiraph_available) + ggtitle("Raw")
pca.qc <- PlotPCA(GetPCA(qc_data), interactive = ggiraph_available) + ggtitle("QC")
pca.rm <- PlotPCA(GetPCA(rm_data), interactive = ggiraph_available) +
  ggtitle("Missingness removed")

pcas <- list(pca.raw, pca.qc, pca.rm) |> wrap_plots(nrow = 3, guides = "collect")

if (ggiraph_available) ggiraph::girafe(pcas) else pcas

Imputation 

imputed_data <- impute.QRILC(rm_data)

Model fitting 

groups <- unique(imputed_data$Group)

results <- DiffMetabolites(imputed_data)

PlotVolcano(results, groups[c(1, 5)], contrastTitle = "Example")

As with the PCA plots, setting interactive = TRUE produces interactive volcano plots:

all_volcanoes <- PlotAllVolcanoes(
  results,
  groups[c(1:3)],
  contrastTitle = "Example",
  interactive = ggiraph_available) |>
  wrap_plots(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "top")

if (ggiraph_available) ggiraph::girafe(all_volcanoes) else all_volcanoes

Pipeline 

fc_data <- ReadFile(exdata_path) |>
  QCData() |>
  RemoveMissing() |>
  impute.QRILC() |>
  DiffMetabolites()
